svg.text: How a request travels from the browser to the GPU
The UI is static files on CloudFront. Its API calls ride a VPC-attached Lambda to the orchestrator, which has no public address.
The orchestrator runs the six bidding containers in four stages; four of the six call NVIDIA Triton on the GPU node.
signs in with Cognito, loads the
static app, exchanges the ID token
serves the frontend as static files;
no API traffic passes through it
user pool signs the browser in;
identity pool grants it one action:
lambda:InvokeFunction, SigV4-signed, bearer token carried unchanged
http://<internal NLB> (orchestrator-internal Service; nothing here is reachable from the internet)
Verifies the Cognito token, then runs the request through four sequential stages, applying each stage's mutations to a working copy before the next stage runs.
gives each stage the time left under tmax
(floored at 10 ms); a slow container is
reported timeout and the next stage still runs
writes segments, deals, metrics and floors
onto the working copy between stages;
four stages, in order; containers inside a stage run in parallel
SIX ARTF CONTAINERS (EKS, CPU NODE GROUP)
runs only when a bid response is sent
NVIDIA Triton Inference Server (GPU node group, g5 / A10G)
Behind an internal-only load balancer. Serves two TensorRT engines (DLRM, NCF) and two XGBoost models (floor, margin) from one GPU.
The node group scales to zero on a nightly schedule. Stage 1 never touches the GPU; stages 2 to 4 make four GPU calls per request.
